 **Measure of National Income**
 
 **Formula**

options.text: i - b, ii - d, iii - a, iv - c
i - a, ii - c, iii - d, iv - b
i - d, ii - a, iii - b, iv - c

solution:
The correct answer is__** i - d, ii - a, iii - b, iv - c.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GNP:-**

 
 
• Gross National Product is the total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, including those produced abroad, and can be calculated as C (consumption) + I (investment) + G (government spending) + net exports (exports - imports).
 
 
 
• **NNP:-**
 
 
• (Net National Product) is the GNP minus depreciation, which is the decrease in value of capital goods over time due to wear and tear.
 
 
 
• **GDP:-**
 
 
• (Gross Domestic Product) is the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders, and can be calculated as C + I + G + net exports.
 
 
 
• **NDP:-**
 
 
• (Net Domestic Product) is the GDP minus depreciation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National income measures:-**

 
 
• These are important indicators of a country's economic performance and are used for policy-making and analysis.
 
• Another measure of national income is GNI (Gross National Income), which is similar to GNP but includes net income from abroad and excludes net taxes and subsidies.
 
• Per capita measures of national income, such as GDP per capita or GNP per capita, can provide insights into the standard of living of a country's population.
 
• National income measures have limitations and do not capture important aspects of economic activity, such as non-market activities, informal sector, and environmental degradation.
